correctness.rationale: The four predecessor-pair relation construction gives an exact if-and-only-if criterion for periodic output membership, allowing an input predecessor whose period is a multiple of the output period. Counting labeled word products via the fully reachable finite Boolean-relation system gives P_r(n)=e T_r^n f_r for every positive n. The packaged verifier checks the entire 256-rule catalog, each rule-specific integer recurrence at N consecutive indices where N is its reachable transition-state count, and the shared initial values for each claimed class. Cayley-Hamilton extends those exact tests to all periods. All 31 class fingerprints are pairwise distinct in their first eight terms, and Rules 7 and 25 agree through seven but not eight. A separate n-phase graph checks all length-1..8 output words. Remaining risk: independently rerun and inspect the supplied code and certificate construction.

value.rationale: Artin–Mazur zeta functions and spatial periodic-point counts are established conjugacy invariants, and the complete ECA family is a natural finite universality class. The result compresses 256 nontrivial infinite sequences into exactly 31 exact types and gives an unusually strong, sharp eight-count criterion for equality of all future counts. The rules 7 and 25 exhibit genuine seven-period indistinguishability and an eight-period split, ruling out arbitrary cutoff selection. This answers a natural complete classification question rather than a routine isolated case, while explicitly making no claim to classify conjugacy or temporal dynamics.
